mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages indicates a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered regimes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which supports corporate revenue and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, in the absence of a corresponding drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals underreported labor market weakness, which presages negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls >1% MoM AND UNRATE does not rise >0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than GDPC1) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows >2% MoM while GDPC1 grows <1% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.
